1

These Civil Miscellaneous Appeals are filed by the appellants, challenging the common order dated 27.03.2015 passed in M.C.O.P.Nos.1537, 1538 & 1539 of 2012 on the file of III Additional Sub Court,
Trichy.
2.Since all the appeals arise out of the claim petitions filed by the injured persons, who had suffered injuries in the same accident, they are taken up together.

3.The appellants (3 in number) had filed the claim petitions, stating that on 09.06.2012, while they were travelling in a two wheeler, the vehicle insured with the 2nd respondent came in the opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the bike, which resulted in serious injuries to the rider of the two wheeler, who is the claimant in C.M.A.(MD)No.934 of 2018 and caused injuries to the other two claimants.
The claim petitions were tried together.
4.The claimants examined four witnesses and marked Ex.P.1 to P.11.
The 2nd respondent had neither examined any witnesses nor marked any documents.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis C.M.A(MD)Nos.932 to 934 of 2018

5.The Tribunal, after considering the oral and documentary evidence, had determined the compensation payable as Rs.16,427/- to the claimant in C.M.A.(MD)No.932 of 2018, a sum of Rs.16,718 to the claimant in C.M.A. (MD)No.933 of 2018 and a sum of Rs.3,13,807/- to the claimant in C.M.A. (MD)No.934 of 2018 and after deducting 50% towards contributory negligence, had directed the 2nd respondent to pay half of the aforesaid amount to the claimants.
6.The learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the only grievance of the appellants is that the Tribunal had apportioned 50% contributory negligence on the claimants, on the sole ground that three persons travelled in the two wheeler, without discussing the exact manner of the occurrence and that hence, the said finding requires modification.
7.The learned counsel has further submitted that though the Doctor had assessed disability at 49%,
in respect of the claimant in C.M.A.(MD)No. 934 of 2018, the Tribunal, without any basis, had reduced the disability to 45%.
8.The 1st respondent remained ex-parte before the Tribunal and though notice was served and the learned counsel has entered appearance for the 1st respondent, there is no representation today.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis C.M.A(MD)Nos.932 to 934 of 2018 9.The learned counsel for the 2nd respondent, per contra, has submitted that the manner of the accident would show that the claimants are also equally responsible for the accident and the contributory negligence fixed by the Tribunal cannot be faulted with and that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
Therefore, the award may be confirmed.

10.The points for consideration in the instant appeal are as follows:-

sentences.text: (A)Whether the Tribunal was right in fixing 50% contributory negligence on the claimants for triples riding?; and (B)Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?.

11.As regards the first point, it is seen that the claimants had examined themselves to prove that the accident occurred only due to a rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The respondents had not let in any contra evidence to disprove the version of the claimants.
The only basis, on which the contributory negligence was fixed on the claimants, is that three persons travelled in the bike.

12.This Court is of the view that merely because three persons were in the bike, it cannot be said that they contributed to the accident in equal https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis C.M.A(MD)Nos.932 to 934 of 2018 measure.
The act of the claimants is certainly a violation.

However, in the absence of any evidence to prove that the rider of the two wheeler or the fact that three persons travelled had contributed to the accident, the contributory negligence at 50% cannot be fixed.
However, this Court is of the view that in view of the violation, it would be reasonable to fix 10% contributory negligence on all three claimants.
Hence, the first point is answered accordingly.

13.As regards the quantum of compensation, this Court finds that the claimants in C.M.A.(MD)Nos.932 and 933 of 2018 have been awarded just and reasonable compensation and therefore, the same deserves to be confirmed.
14.As regards the claimant in C.M.A.(MD)No.934 of 2018, this Court finds that though the Doctor had assessed the disability at 49%, there was no basis for the Tribunal to reduce it to 45%.

Hence,
the compensation under the head of disability is enhanced to 49% and the amount under the head of disability comes to Rs.1,47,000/- (49 X 3000).

Therefore, the compensation payable to the claimant in C.M.A.(MD)No.934 of 2018 is modified as follows:-

2nd respondent Insurance Company is directed to deposit the award amount modified by this Court together with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realization (excluding the period of dismissal for default if any) and costs, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

17.On such deposit, the claimants are permitted to withdraw the same, less the amount, if any,
already withdrawn, by filing an appropriate application before the Tribunal.
18.In the result
, these Civil Miscellaneous Appeals are partly allowed.
No costs.
